notes: 3 positive cases (must fire the skill) + 4 negative ones (must route to skill-creator, senior-prompt-engineer or /design-fix). Schema copied from ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/deploy/evals/evals.json.
runner: ALWAYS run case by case with --test-case; NEVER in default mode. In default mode the runner flattens the assertions of every case against a single response, and then `contains: harness-audit` (positive) and `not_contains: harness-audit` (negative) cancel each other out — the mathematical ceiling lands around 81%, below any useful threshold. Measured 2026-08-17: default = 75%, 4 critical failures, exit 1, with the correct artefacts.

evals.prompt: Are my commands, skills and agents inside .claude connected and calling each other correctly?
evals.expected_output: Invokes harness-audit, builds the inventory and wiring graph (graph.json), classifies dangling references / orphans / cycles with path:line, dispatches skill-improver in an isolated subagent for the verdict, and stops without applying a patch.

assertions.description: The harness-audit skill is invoked, not skill-creator.
Produces a wiring graph whose edges cite path:line at both ends.
The verdict comes from an isolated subagent, not from the gathering itself.
Explicitly states that it stopped without applying a patch.
assertions.note: A POSITIVE check of the stop, not `not_contains: "patch applied"` — that one fires precisely on the correct report ("no patch applied"), because the negation contains the forbidden string itself. Measured 2026-08-17: 75%, exit 1, with the right behaviour. Same family as `contains: ls`: a substring that matches the opposite of what it means to detect.

evals.prompt: A skill in my repository fires at the wrong time and sometimes loads content from a global skill of the same name. What is going on?
evals.expected_output: Invokes harness-audit, runs Phase 3 (shadowing), applies enterprise > personal > project precedence, compares the repository's name values against ~/.claude/skills, proves which file the listing serves by comparing the two descriptions, classifies it P0 when the losing version is the repository's authority, and proposes a rename without applying it.

assertions.description: Identifies enterprise > personal > project precedence as the cause.
Compares the two same-named files instead of assuming which one wins.
Proposes a patch (rename the repository's skill or remove the global one) without applying it.

evals.prompt: One of my commands calls a subagent the CLI says it cannot find. Check everything: agents, skills, commands and workflows.
evals.expected_output: Invokes harness-audit, tests the four silent resolvers (symlink, precedence, agentRouting.aliases map, module importer) and reopens the disk (`ls `, `grep `, Glob) before confirming anything dangles, then grades severity by call site (it executes = P0; a name inside an illustrative code block = P3).

assertions.description: Checks agentRouting.aliases before declaring the name dangling.
Reopens the disk instead of trusting the text of the calling command.
assertions.note: The word boundary is what kills the false positive: `\bls ` matches neither "skills " (the `l` is preceded by `l`, so there is no boundary) nor "aliases"/"false". The first attempt used `ls -`, which turned into a false negative — it did not match the real report, which writes `ls ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/...` with no flag. Tested in both directions on 2026-08-17.

assertions.description: Distinguishes a name inside an illustrative code block from a live call site.

evals.prompt: Create a skill for handling file attachment uploads.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke harness-audit. Routes to skill-creator, the skill for creating or iterating on ONE skill.

evals.prompt: Improve the debugger agent's prompt so it stops proposing a fix before it has found the root cause.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke harness-audit. Routes to senior-prompt-engineer, the owner of the shape contract for .claude/agents/*.md.

evals.prompt: My deploy skill does not fire when I ask for a deploy. How do I make it fire?
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke harness-audit. This is description tuning for ONE skill — skill-creator territory, and skill-creator claims 'my skill isn't triggering' in its own description. harness-audit only enters when the question is about the link between artefacts (trigger collision across N skills, repo-versus-global shadowing).

assertions.description: harness-audit is not invoked for tuning a single description.

evals.note: Case added 2026-08-17 after dogfooding showed this is the exact prompt where harness-audit and skill-creator collide, and no eval covered it.

evals.prompt: Refactor the inventory-table component — it is too big and it breaks on mobile.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke harness-audit — this is application source code, outside the harness scope. Routes to /design-fix or frontend-specialist.

assertions.description: Recognises application source code as outside the harness scope.
